2. The respondents instituted the original suit as plaintiffs for declaration of title to the suit land in the schedule of the plant and subsequently by amendment of the plaint also prayed for recovery of khas possession on alleging that the land measuring 19½ decimals appertaining to mouza-Bagura Alekanda in J.L. No.50 under C.S. Khatian Nos.160 and 178, Plot No.1548 belonged to Gobinda Shil: He executed a will and appointed his wife-Sona Lakhsmi as executrix. Defendant No.3, Ramesh Chandra Shil, was the next reversioner. After the death of Gobinda Chandra Shil, Sona Lakhsmi filed Probate Case No.6 of 1917 before the District Judge, Barisal. Sona Lakhsmi and the reversionar heir leased out the said land to Dinabandhu Gangopadhya (father of defendant Nos.1 and 2) by patta dated 05.11.1941 for legal necessity and delivered possession thereof. In the said patta by mistake Plot No.1549 was written instead of Plot No.1548, but the boundary and the area of the land were correctly written. Since the said pattan, defendant Nos.1 and 2 had been residing on the suit land by constructing dwelling structures thereon on payment of rent, municipal tax etc. The said defendants transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by registered sale deed dated 12.05.1970, but in that sale deed also mistakenly Plot No.1549 was written in lieu of Plot No.1548. During R.S. operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother-Sona Lakhsmi although they had never claimed the same. Husband of defendant No.6 in collusion with Sudhir Chandra Dutta, an employee of defendant No.5, constructed structures on Plot No.804, and as such, the plaint was amended incorporating prayer for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'lcha' scheduled land. The collusively pre-pared wrong record in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother has clouded the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant No.6 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the plaint case contending, inter alia, that Sona Lakhshmi Shil and her next reversioner did not execute and register the alleged patta dated 05.11.1941 in favour of defendant Nos. l and 2 and no such patta was acted upon. Dinobundhu Gangopadhya or his heirs, defendant Nos.l and 2 never possessed the suit land. The land of CS Plot No.1549 has been recorded in RS Plot Nos.798-803/2001-2004. Manindra and others owned the suit land in Mirash ejara right. Plot No.1548 was possessed by temporary lessees of Sona Lakhshmi, named Bipin Behari, Abdul Aziz, Hiron Kumar Karmakar and three other persons. Defendant No.5 attempted to acquire the land of temporary tenant, Abdul Aziz. When landlord Ramesh Chandra Shil attempted to make the land khas, defendant No.5 took settlement on 29.12.1945 in Mirash ejara right of the land of Plot No.1548 and as he failed to get khas possession of the entire property, he gradually purchased the interests of temporary tenants and obtained khas possession of the suit land. Defendant No.5 made constructions in the suit land, opened municipal holding and mutated the property in his name and in the name of his wife and inducted tenants therein on monthly rental basis. Defendant No.5 and his wife transferred 0.431 acre land including the suit land to defendant No.6 by a registered sale deed dated 01.09.1969 at a consideration of taka 6,000.00. After purchase, defendant No.6 mutated her name in the revenue records and in the municipality in respect of the land and constructing structures thereon, she has been possessing some part of the suit land herself along with the members of her family and some parts through the monthly tenants. The plaintiffs have no title, interest and possession in the suit land, and they have filed the suit to grab the same creation forged maner and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 10. The plaintiffs (respondents) have come with an allegation that Sona Lakhsmi and the next reversioner heir leased out the aforementioned land to one Dinabandhu Gangopadhya who is the father of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by patta dated 05.11.1941 for mitigating her legal necessity and delivered possession thereof and in that patta by mistake Plot No.1549 was written instead of Plot No.1548, but the boundaries and area of land were correctly written. It has been further alleged that after the death of Dinabandhu Gangopadhya, the suit land devolved upon defendant Nos.1 and 2 as his heirs who as owner in possession transferred the same to the plaintiff (respondent) by a kabala deed dated 12.05.1970 wherein Plot No.1549 was written in lieu of Plot No.1548 erroneously. It has been also alleged that the husband of defendant No.6 in collusion with an employee of defendant No.5 illegally constructed structures on Plot No.804 and as such, the plaint was amended incorporating prayer for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'Kha' scheduled land. 

 11. On the other hand, the contesting defendant No.6(who is appellant here) denied the aforesaid allegation of the plaintiff and counter claimed that Sona Lakhsmi and others never executed any patta as alleged nor the same was acted upon and not only the plaintiffs but also their predecessor never possessed the said land as alleged and accordingly, the RS Khatian has been prepared in the name of Sona Lakhsmi, whose temporary lessee Bipin Behari, Abdul Aziz and Hiron Kumar Karmaker have been possessing the land in Plot No.1548. It has been further alleged that defendant No.5 took settlement of the suit land from Ramesh Chandra Shil on 29.12.1945 and took the same in his khas possession and thereafter transferred 0.431 acres land in favour of defendant  No.6 by kabala dated 01.09.1969 who mutated her name in suit khatian and has been possessing the same on constructing structures thereon. 

 13. It is the positive case of the plaintiffs (respondents herein) that Sona Lakhsmi and her next reversioner settled the suit land to one Dinabandhu Gangopadhya by patta dated 05.11.1941 and his legal heirs subsequently transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffs(respondents) by kabala dated 12.05.1970. Now, the main dispute that falls for determination is whether any tenancy right had been created in favour of Dinabandhu Gangopadhya under the landlord-Sona Lakhsmi and others. A patta is an unilateral document through which a tenancy could be created whenever the tenant obtained rent receipt on payment of rent to the landlord and the landlord granted such type of rent receipt from their Zamindary sheresta which are private in nature. 

 15. Section 101 of the evidence Act makes it obligatory upon the plaintiff of a civil action to prove the existence of the fact on which he bases his claim. In the instant case, the plaintiff based his claim on the basis of patta dated 05.11.1941 which is an instrument of unitary in nature. With a view to create a tenancy right in favour of Dinabandhu Gangopadhya under land-lord-Sona Lakhsmi, the plaintiffs are to show that Sona Lakhsmi duly granted rent receipt on acknowledging rent in favour of tenant. One Abdul Mannan was examined as PW1 in this case who deposed that he is a man of 52 years and his date of birth is 23.10.1937. Thus, it appears that at the time of alleged patta settlement, he was mere a child and he had no personal knowledge about such settlement. PW2, Hamid Mallick and PW3, Ali Ashraf are the witnesses who have come before the Court to depose in respect of the plaintiffs' possession and subsequent kabala purchase in favour of the plaintiffs and they uttered nothing about alleged patta settlement. PW1, Abdul Mannan deposed that Dinabandhu Gangopadhya gave rent in favour of Ramesh and Sona Lakhsmi. He further deposed that he has filed rent receipt with a view to show the fact of such payment of rent, but he failed to depose as to the fact that for which number of plot Dinabandhu Gangopadhya paid the rent. In fact, no such rent receipts were being exhibited by the trial Court during the course of trial. Mere filing of the private dakhila without formal proof thereof and without proving the contents of such document cannot fulfill the requirement. 

 16. The evidentiary value of those private document can only be evaluated on the basis of adduced evidence by the plaintiffs (respondents). But in the instant case, the plaintiff-respondent neither produced the writer of those private dakhila nor produced any person in whose presence that was written with a view to prove the same. Thus, we have no other alternative but to hold that the plaintiff failed to prove the private dakhila or its content on adducing proper and competent witness. After preparation of SA record of right more than 50/60 years have been elapsed, the plaintiffs (respondents) failed to correct or mutate their names in the suit khatian on the strength of such patta and alleged private rent receipts. From the order sheet dated 09.12.1970 in Bakarganj district mutation case bearing No.179kt of 1957-58, it appears that plaintiff-Abdul Quddus filed the mutation case before the concerned Revenue Circle Officer, Kotwali, Barishal who rejected the mutation objection case on holding that the objector, Abdul Quddus has got no locus standi to file the mutation objection. It is fact that if the plaintiffs (respondents) had really been the custodian of those private dakhilas in that case, they might have submitted the same before the Revenue Circle Officer, but they failed to produce those dakhilas before such officer. Failure to submit those private dakhilas before the Revenue Circle Officer, raised an apprehension as to whether the plaintiffs or their predecessor was at all the custodian of those private documents. 

 19. In spite of that the learned Judge of the High Court Division travelled beyond the scope of the revision in making the Rule absolute and sending the suit back on remand to the trial Court for hearing afresh although both the Courts of fact have arrived at a concurrent finding of fact that the plaintiffs (respondents) have failed to prove their right, title, interest and possession in RS Plot No.1548 tracing back their title therein through the patta dated 05.11.1941. 

 21. We further hold that erroneous insertion of plot number in the disputed patta as well as the plaintiffs' kabala is a long pending dispute which could be corrected on filing a case for rectification of those deeds but the plaintiffs (respondents) sat idle for more than 50 years without taking such type of steps.
